newsitem.title: UK: Smith & Nephew helped by upbeat broker talk. [CORRECTED 11:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Smith & Nephew helped by upbeat broker talk. [CORRECTED 11:10 GMT]

text.p: Shares in healthcare group Smith & Nephew Plc ignored a market downtrend, trading unchanged at 179 pence following positive comments from NatWest Markets, dealers said.
The broker upgraded the shares to "hold" from "reduce" (corrects recommendation from "undervalued" to "reduce"), they added. NatWest' analysts declined to comment.

Smith & Nephew reported lower first-half results last week, but many analysts are optimistic about the group's long-term prospects, expecting a strong profit contribution from new skin graft product Dermagraft after the year 2000.
Smith & Nephew earlier announced it had received approval to market Dermagraft for treatment of diabetic foot ulcers in Canada.
